solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Merge with traffic passing around one vehicle creating obstruction (10)

indicatorNotes.passing around: FILTER passes around the others, so they sit inside it

blocks.note: to filter is to merge into a traffic lane

annotation.surface: A driver edging into a lane of traffic finds a single vehicle blocking the way.
annotation.walkthrough: The traffic picture makes 'obstruction' look like a stalled car; it is the parliamentary kind, a filibuster being a speech spun out to block a vote.
annotation.definitionFit: A filibuster is a tactic of obstruction, delaying legislation by talking at length.

entries.clue: Wink hidden by German contractor almost noted (6)

indicatorNotes.hidden by: MO is covered up by the other word, so it goes inside it
indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word: the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: FAUST, the German scholar who made a contract with the devil, without his last letter
a wink is an instant, a mo

annotation.surface: A German builder cuts corners while someone winks behind his back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contractor' reads as a builder, but it is Faust, who signed a contract with the devil in the German legend.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone noted is well known, that is famous.

entries.clue: Soft shell from extinct mollusc (6)

indicatorNotes.shell from: the shell of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A fossil hunter describes the soft remains of a long-dead shellfish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shell' belongs so naturally with 'mollusc' that it reads as the animal's shell; here it takes the outside letters of 'extinct'.
annotation.definitionFit: A limpet is a sea mollusc that clings to rocks.

entries.clue: Car and bike adverts edited, being full of unwanted advice (4-4,6)

indicatorNotes.edited: edited text is rearranged, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters; 'and' joins the pieces

annotation.surface: Motoring ads are cut about until they are stuffed with advice nobody asked for.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb, but it is a noun here: a being, a person, full of unwanted advice.
annotation.definitionFit: A back-seat driver is someone who offers unwanted advice, like a passenger telling the driver how to drive.

entries.clue: Pressure auction houses with offer about new charm (9)

indicatorNotes.houses: SELL houses P, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.about: BID goes about N, around it

blocks.note: a bid is an offer at auction

annotation.surface: Pushy auctioneers use offers to talk up some new trinket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Auction houses' looks like a single noun, Sotheby's and the like; split, 'houses' is a verb and does the containing.
annotation.definitionFit: To charm someone can mean to hold them under a spell, to spellbind them.

entries.clue: Clear up last speck of dust in vent (5)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

annotation.surface: A housekeeper chases the final speck of dust out of an air vent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vent' sits in the surface as an air grille, but the definition is the verb: to vent is to burst out, as a volcano does.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a volcano both vents and erupts, each meaning to burst out forcefully.

entries.clue: Cry weakly ignoring a passing idea (4)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: the word leaves out the item named

blocks.note: to whimper is to cry weakly
per = a, as in 'ten pounds a head'; this is removed

annotation.surface: Someone sniffles and lets a fleeting thought slip by.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A' does more work than it looks: it stands for PER, as in 'twice a day'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a whim is a fancy that comes and goes, an idea that soon passes.

entries.clue: Hearts go faster wanting male repeatedly in secret (4-4)

indicatorNotes.wanting: wanting means lacking, so M is taken out
indicatorNotes.repeatedly: something done repeatedly happens again, so the whole H+USH unit is written a second time

blocks.note: MUSH, the cry urging sled dogs to go faster, without M for male

annotation.surface: Pulses race, over and over, in some clandestine affair.
annotation.walkthrough: Mush is the musher's command to sled dogs to get moving; 'repeatedly' doubles the whole H+USH unit.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal doubled synonym: repeating 'hush' makes an adjective for what must be kept quiet.

entries.clue: Additional meat for member of parliament? (8)

annotation.surface: An MP helps himself to a second helping of meat.
annotation.walkthrough: The member of parliament is no politician: a group of owls is called a parliament, and the morepork is a New Zealand owl. The question mark flags the trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A morepork is an owl, and owls gather in a parliament.

entries.clue: Criminal Capone can let us behave better (5,2,4,3)

indicatorNotes.Criminal: criminal means corrupt, twisted, so the letters are bent out of order

annotation.surface: Al Capone, the gangster, might allow us to mend our ways.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' seems to describe Capone, the Chicago gangster; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: cleaning up one's act means reforming one's conduct.

entries.clue: Setter’s reflecting on note about “parrot” (5)

indicatorNotes.reflecting: a reflection shows a thing reversed
indicatorNotes.about: about in its sense of approximately is circa, abbreviated C

blocks.note: the setter is I; setter's = I'M, reversed
mi, the third note of the scale

annotation.surface: A crossword setter muses over a note written about a parrot.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter is I in crosswords, so 'setter's' is I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a parrot's copying of speech gives the verb its sense of imitating.

entries.clue: Heat in Washington Square deli’s awful, needing day off (9)

indicatorNotes.awful: something awful is a mess, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.off: a day off is a day taken away, so D comes off DELI

blocks.note: D = day, the letter taken off DELI
's = is, surface glue joining the fodder to its indicator

annotation.surface: A heatwave in Washington Square, and the deli there is terrible and should close for the day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heat' is US slang for a gun, and so is equaliser; Washington flags the American usage. 'Washington Square' is a famous New York park, pulling the capital out of view.
annotation.definitionFit: In American slang both heat and equaliser mean a gun.

entries.clue: Tune is ruined by large instrument (7)

indicatorNotes.ruined: a ruined thing is wrecked, its letters knocked about

annotation.surface: A melody is spoilt by some big, loud musical instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tune' and 'instrument' set up a music scene; the instrument is a kitchen tool.
annotation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or instrument, especially in the kitchen.

entries.clue: Kid finishing early with hard work in cafe (3,4)

indicatorNotes.finishing early: the word stops a letter short, losing its end

blocks.note: TEASE = kid, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A child knocks off early after a spell of hard graft at a cafe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child; it is the verb, to tease.
annotation.definitionFit: A tea shop is a small cafe serving tea and light meals.

entries.clue: Roughly boxing in clubs, fighter shows craft (5,7)

indicatorNotes.boxing: BRUISER boxes the letters, holding them in a box around them

blocks.note: a bruiser is a tough fighter

annotation.surface: A boxer sparring at local clubs shows some rough skill in the ring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' and 'fighter' make a boxing scene, and 'craft' reads as skill; it is a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A cabin cruiser is a motor boat with living quarters, a craft.

entries.clue: Children given a model insect with a changing lustre (9)

blocks.note: a model car or train is a toy

annotation.surface: Children get a model bug with a shimmering, iridescent coat.
annotation.walkthrough: Chatoyant, from the French for a cat's eye, describes a stone whose sheen shifts like a cat's eye.
annotation.definitionFit: Chatoyant means having a changeable lustre, like a cat's-eye gem.

entries.clue: Warm jams leak out slowly on the surface (4-4)

indicatorNotes.jams: KIND is jammed into SEEP, wedged inside it

blocks.note: to seep is to leak out slowly

annotation.surface: Warm jam oozes gradually over the top of something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jams' looks like the fruit preserve; it is the verb, to jam or cram in.
annotation.definitionFit: Something skin-deep is superficial, only on the surface.

entries.clue: Adult film contains party gatecrashed by maiden right in the centre (8)

indicatorNotes.contains: MIST holds the next piece inside it
indicatorNotes.gatecrashed by: a gatecrasher gets inside the party uninvited, so M goes into DO

blocks.note: a film of mist, a thin layer
M = maiden, a cricket over with no runs

annotation.surface: An X-rated film features a party crashed by a young woman, right at its heart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Adult film' reads as a single phrase; split, 'adult' is A and 'film' is MIST. Maiden = M comes from cricket scoring.
annotation.definitionFit: Amidmost is an old word for in the very middle.

entries.clue: Monitor a thousand old government officials taking too much on, including newspaper (6,6)

indicatorNotes.including: OD ON includes RAG, taking it in

blocks.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper

annotation.surface: A watchdog keeps an eye on a thousand officials of a former government who overreached, press included.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Monitor' looks like a verb to watch over; it is a noun, the monitor lizard, of which the Komodo dragon is the largest.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the largest monitor lizard of all is this Indonesian giant.

entries.clue: Drawer in cart is tiny (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is found in the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundaries of these three words

annotation.surface: A drawer inside a cart is very small.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' reads as a sliding box in furniture; it is one who draws.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-favourite sense: a drawer is one who draws pictures, as any sketching painter does.

entries.clue: Drink up glass of beer first giving unintelligible speech (6)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means written bottom to top
indicatorNotes.first: JAR is placed at the front

blocks.note: a jar is a pint of beer

annotation.surface: Downing a pint first leaves someone's speech slurred.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drink up' reads as an order to finish a glass; it is a drink, NOG, flipped. A jar is British slang for a glass of beer.
annotation.definitionFit: Jargon is specialist language that outsiders find unintelligible.

entries.clue: Footage of interviewer put on the wrong way cuts out (7)

indicatorNotes.the wrong way: something put on the wrong way round is back to front, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: DON = put on, as of clothes, backwards
an engine that cuts out dies

annotation.surface: An editor complains that the interview footage was put in back to front and cuts out.
annotation.walkthrough: Noddies are the TV cutaway shots of an interviewer nodding, filmed afterwards and edited in.
annotation.definitionFit: Noddies are shots of an interviewer nodding, edited into interview footage.

entries.clue: Period set aside for mourning deity (5)

blocks.note: the Jewish week of mourning after a funeral

annotation.surface: A time is set aside to mourn a god.
annotation.walkthrough: Two unrelated words share a spelling: the Hebrew shiva, seven days of mourning, and the Sanskrit name of the Hindu god.
annotation.definitionFit: Sitting shiva is the Jewish mourning period; Shiva is a principal Hindu deity.

entries.clue: Evergreen song accompanying cheer at World Cup (7)

blocks.note: an aria is a song in opera

annotation.surface: A classic song belted out alongside the chants at a World Cup match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen song' reads as a golden oldie; the evergreen is the olearia, or daisy bush, and 'accompanying' only sets OLE beside ARIA.
annotation.definitionFit: Olearia, the daisy bush, is an evergreen shrub.

entries.clue: Mysterious secret objects and information primarily (9)

annotation.definition: Mysterious secret objects and information primarily

indicatorNotes.Mysterious: a mysterious arrangement is obscure, so the letters are scrambled
indicatorNotes.primarily: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: the first letters of Objects And Information

annotation.surface: A description of arcane secret things and knowledge.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: esoterica are mysterious secret objects and information.
annotation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure items or knowledge understood only by a few.

entries.clue: Giving weapon to marine becoming cross leads to dismissal (5)

indicatorNotes.becoming: one piece turns into another, replacing it

blocks.note: arming someone gives them a weapon
RM, a Royal Marine, replaced by X, a cross

annotation.surface: Handing a gun to a marine who is angry gets him fired.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the letter X. RM stands for Royal Marine.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal, headline-writer's synonym: the axe falls on a job when someone is sacked.

entries.clue: US idiot attempts to complete course over the phone (4)

indicatorNotes.over the phone: on the phone you only hear a word, so it is a sound-alike

blocks.note: putts are the strokes a golfer plays to finish a hole

annotation.surface: An American fool tries to finish a golf course while chatting on his phone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a golf course, and the attempts to complete a hole are putts.
annotation.definitionFit: Putz is American slang, from Yiddish, for a fool.

entries.clue: Pastry paintings gallery sent back inside container (5,5)

indicatorNotes.sent back: the word is turned back to front
indicatorNotes.inside: inside means within, so ART and ETAT sit within the container word

annotation.surface: Paintings are returned to a gallery packed in a crate, alongside a pastry.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tate is the London art gallery.
annotation.definitionFit: Tarte Tatin is an upside-down caramelised apple tart.
